chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir narrated from his father, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: Why did Allah forbid wine, carrion, blood, and the flesh of swine? So he said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not forbid that to His servants and permit what is beyond that out of desire for what He made lawful for them, nor out of disregard for what He made forbidden to them. Rather, He, Mighty and Majestic, created creation and knew what their bodies are sustained by and what benefits them, so He made it lawful for them and allowed it for them. And He knew what harms them, so He forbade them from it. Then He made it lawful for the one compelled by necessity at the time in which his body cannot subsist except by it, so He commanded him to take from it only to the measure of bare sufficiency, nothing beyond that.”

Then he said: “As for carrion, no one partakes of it except that his body becomes weak, his strength declines, and his offspring are cut off; and the eater of carrion does not die except suddenly. As for blood, it causes the one who consumes it to develop yellow fluid disease, to inherit savagery, hardness of heart, and little tenderness and mercy, until he is not trusted with his close relation nor trusted with one who accompanies him. As for the flesh of swine, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, transformed a people into various forms such as swine, apes, and bears; then He forbade eating the transformed creatures so that no benefit be taken from them and so that their punishment not be made light of. As for wine, He forbade it because of its effects and its corruption.”

Then he said: “Indeed, the habitual drinker of wine is like an idol-worshipper. It causes trembling in him, destroys his dignity, and drives him to dare against the forbidden matters, such as shedding blood and committing zina, until it cannot be trusted, when he is intoxicated, that he may not assault his own protected household while not perceiving that. And wine increases its drinker in nothing but every evil.”

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood; forbidden substance described as causing physical and moral corruption
key_terms.الْبُلْغَةِ: bare sufficiency; the minimum amount needed for survival
key_terms.الْخَمْرَ: wine; an intoxicant forbidden because of its harmful effects and corruption
key_terms.الْمَحَارِمِ: forbidden matters; sacred limits violated under intoxication
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةَ: carrion; dead meat forbidden for its bodily harm
key_terms.الْمُضْطَرِّ: the one compelled by necessity; a person permitted to consume the forbidden only to the extent needed
key_terms.لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ: the flesh of swine; forbidden and linked here to transformed creatures
key_terms.مُدْمِنَ الْخَمْرِ: habitual drinker of wine; described as spiritually and morally degraded

ai.seo_question: Why did Allah forbid wine, carrion, blood, and pork in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, forbids certain things not arbitrarily, but because of His knowledge of what benefits and harms His servants. It also clarifies the concession of necessity and describes the physical, moral, and social فساد associated with carrion, blood, swine flesh, and especially wine.
